This matter is taken up through Hybrid Arrangement (Virtual/Physical Mode).
2.

This is a bail application U/S.439 of Cr.P.C. by the petitioner for grant of bail in connection with Padwa P.S. Case No. 118 of 2022 corresponding to G.R. Case No.975 of 2022 pending in the file of learned S.D.J.M., Koraput being charge sheeted for commission of offences punishable under Sections 376/506/454/354- A(1)(ii) of the IPC, on the main allegation of committing rape upon the victim.
3. Heard, Mr. D.R. Bhokta, learned counsel for the Petitioner and Mr. S.R. Roul, learned ASC in the matter and perused the record.

It is brought to the notice of the Court that the victim has also earlier lodged an F.I.R. against the petitioner on 07.12.2023, wherein she has not narrated any allegation of rape against the petitioner, even though the occurrence in the present case is stated to have been occurred on 17th November, 2022 in the F.I.R/ 17th October, 2022 in 161 statement of the victim.
It is also brought to the notice of the Court that the victim has refused to undergo medical examination.

4. In view of the above facts and taking into consideration the rival submissions and on going through the materials placed on record and the facts stated in the preceding paragraph with regard to the lodging of F.I.R. without indicating therein about the commission of rape upon the victim,
even though by the time of lodging of F.I.R., incident stated to have been already happened and there being no explanation with regard to not indicating the allegation of rape in the earlier F.I.R. by the informant-victim, this Court considers it to be a fit case to exercise its discretion under Section Ajaya Khara vs State Of Odisha ... Opposite Party on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/47468212/
1 439 Cr.P.C.
5. Hence, the bail application of the petitioner stands allowed and the petitioner is allowed to go on bail on furnishing bail bonds of Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand) only with one solvent surety for the like amount to the satisfaction of the learned Court in seisin of the case on such terms and conditions as deem fit and proper by it with following conditions:-
(i) the petitioner shall not commit any offence while on bail,
(ii) the petitioner in the course of trial shall attend the trial Court on each date of posting without fail unless his attendance is dispensed with.

entities.text: Section Ajaya Khara vs State Of Odisha ... Opposite Party on 16 February
entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: In case the Petitioner fails without sufficient cause to appear in the Court in accordance with the terms of the bail, the learned trial Court may proceed against the Petitioner for offence U/S.229-A of IPC in accordance with law, and (iii) the petitioner shall not leave the territorial jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till disposal of the case by intimating his present address of stay

It is clarified that the Court in seisin of the case will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the petitioner without further reference to this Court, if any of the above conditions are violated or a case for cancellation of bail is otherwise made out.

In the wake of aforesaid, the subsequent involvement of the petitioner for offence under grave/similar offence in future on prima facie accusations may be treated as a ground for cancellation of bail.
6. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
7. Issue urgent certified copy of the order as per Rules.
(G. Satapathy) Judge S. Sasmal
